To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the alcoholism generator, which includes fetal, adolescent, and adult exposure to large amounts alcohol, is a major cause of cognitive dysfunction and that this dysfunction can be prevented or reversed by pharmacological and behavioral interventions.
alcoholism and the sequelae are largely caused by a cycle of alcohol-induced cognitive deficits that are generated by alcohol-induced perturbances in neurogenesis and/or synaptogenesis.
alcohol exposure at any developmental stage can cause cognitive dysfunction through mechanisms that are largely mediated by alcohol-induced perturbation of neurogenesis and synapse formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of alcoholism, with the goal of developing effective treatments for alcoholism
the mechanisms of alcohol-induced brain injury and the development of novel treatments to prevent and reverse the effects of alcoholism.

the effects of alcohol and alcoholism on the brain and behavior, with a particular focus on the mechanisms of action of ethanol and the neurobiological and behavioral consequences of fetal, adolescent and adult alcohol exposure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alcoholism generator is the key to understanding and treating problem drinking.
alcohol exposure at any stage of development, especially during adolescence, increases the probability of problem alcohol drinking and cognitive dysfunction.
alcohol exposure at any stage of life can cause cognitive dysfunction through alcohol-induced perturbances in neurogenesis and/or synaptogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified several key molecular and genetic mechanisms that are important for understanding how alcohol can cause cognitive dysfunction.
the alcoholism generator can be broken through the use of the neuroprotective agent, memantine.
alcohol-induced neurodevelopmental disorders are a major cause of alcoholism, and alcohol-induced neurodevelopment disorders and alcoholism are a major cause for alcohol-induced neurodevelopment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are multiple opportunities to intervene to reduce the probability of problem drinking and its consequences.
the alcoholism generator is a self-reinforcing cycle that must be broken to reduce the impact of alcoholism on the individual, family, and society.
